label: Event title: ailment
summary: Gives a title wording for an illness or injury, such as "Brutally Mauled", "Severely Injured", "Injured" or "Ill".
details: It runs on a character and reads two saved scopes: scope:sick_character (checked for the wounded traits) and scope:disease_type (checked for illnesses such as ill and pneumonic). The text names also include gout ridden, leper, typhus, consumption, cancer and lover's pox (listed twice), 18 in all.

label: Experimental brew, childish
summary: Gives a name for a childish brew: a child's name with a brew type, or "<adjective> Small Beer".
details: It runs on a character. It has two texts. One uses the child saved in the variable experimental_brew_child, the other uses the adjective of the character's primary title. It is marked random valid.

label: Experimental brew name
summary: Gives the name of an experimental brew by choosing one of four kinds: negative, childish, positive or very positive.
details: It runs on a character. Vanilla picks by a character flag (experimental_brew_negative, experimental_brew_childish, experimental_brew_positive or experimental_brew_very_positive). Each of its four texts calls another custom text (ExperimentalBrewNegative, ExperimentalBrewChildish, ExperimentalBrewPositive, ExperimentalBrewVeryPositive). It is not random.

label: Experimental brew, bad
summary: Gives a name for a bad brew, such as the character's titled name or the brewmaster's name with a negative adjective and brew type, or a name plus "Mistake".
details: It runs on a character. It has five texts, marked random valid, so the game may pick any of them. The brewmaster is the character saved in the variable experimental_brew_creator. The input shows only four of the five texts.

label: Experimental brew, good
summary: Gives a name for a good brew, such as the character's titled name or the brewmaster's name with a brew type.
details: It runs on a character. It has five texts, marked random valid, so the game may pick any of them. The brewmaster is the character saved in the variable experimental_brew_creator.

label: Experimental brew, excellent
summary: Gives a name for a very good brew, such as the character's titled name or the brewmaster's name with a positive adjective and a brew type.
details: It runs on a character. It has five texts, marked random valid, so the game may pick any of them. The brewmaster is the character saved in the variable experimental_brew_creator.

label: Eye or eyes
summary: Gives the word "eye" for a one-eyed character and "eyes" for everyone else.
details: It runs on a character. Vanilla checks for the one_eyed trait; "eyes" is the fallback. A comment in the file says blind characters still get "eyes".

label: Article or nothing
summary: Gives "a " (with a space) for a one-eyed character and an empty text for everyone else.
details: It runs on a character. Vanilla checks for the one_eyed trait; the empty text is the fallback. It puts "a" in front of "eye" only when the character has just one.

label: French activity name template
summary: Gives the French wording for the full name of an activity: feast, hunt, pilgrimage, tournament, wedding and others.
details: Part of the French text rules, used by the Le, Au and Du helpers in front of the activity's full name. It runs on an activity. It has eleven texts: one per activity type, a fallback, and a first one used when the activity's host is the local player.

label: French activity phase template
summary: Gives the French wording for the current phase of an activity, such as a feast meal or toast, a tournament joust or a wedding ceremony.
details: Part of the French text rules, used by the Le, Du, Au and E helpers for activity phases. It runs on an activity and picks by the activity type and its current phase. It has 24 texts, only the first twelve of which the input shows.

label: French activity short name template
summary: Gives the French wording for the short name of an activity, such as a feast, hunt, pilgrimage or wedding.
details: Part of the French text rules, used by the Le, Au and Du helpers in front of the activity's short name. It runs on an activity. It has ten texts: one per activity type plus a fallback.

label: French on or a for artifact
summary: Gives a French word piece (a female or a male form) that goes in front of an artifact command.
details: Part of the French text rules. It runs on an artifact. Vanilla gives the female form to a list of artifact types (such as dagger, axe, mace, spear, goblet) and the male form to all others. The header note says a space follows it.

label: French de before houses of worship
summary: Gives the French "d" or "de" that goes in front of the plural name of a house of worship.
details: Part of the French text rules. The header note says no space goes after it. It runs on a character and has two texts. Vanilla uses the "d" text for Christianity (except the Bosnian Church) and the Magyar religion, and "de" otherwise.
